observed.facings.png: Three facings on one shared scale. They are the same width and height to within a few percent, so the earlier problem of the north view looking much wider is gone. Each shows a squat brown tortoise-like reptile with a scaly domed shell. On its back sits a large rosette of pointed, leathery leaves, olive to ochre with orange-red edges and yellow centres. Two long dark-maroon stalks rise from the middle of the rosette, each ending in a ribbed, toothed, open trap head.
observed.south.png: Front view. The reptile's head faces the camera under the rim of the leaves: heavy brow, small dark eyes, a stern mouth. Two thick scaly front legs with claws stand on either side, and the back feet show behind them. The leaves fan out wider than the shell. Both trap heads face forward above the leaves. Clean transparent background.
observed.east.png: True side profile facing right. The head and neck stick out on the right below the leaves, with four stout clawed legs underneath. The shell shows striped brown scutes. The rosette covers the top of the shell and its leaves spill past the front and back edges. Two trap stalks curve up and forward at different heights, with their jaws open toward the right. No ground shadow.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The back of the shell, both scaly hind legs with claws, and the flared back rim of the shell are visible. The top of the dome shows just above the centre of the rosette. There is no head, face or eyes. The rosette and both trap stalks match the south view and are mirrored as seen from behind. No visible tail, which is normal for a tortoise. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is a bit shorter than the vanilla human and about one cell long. In normal play at 32 px per cell it reads as an orange-red leafy mass on a brown body with two dark stalks on top, and it stands out clearly from the ground.
